findings.issue: The holder's process name from /proc/<pid>/comm is only trimmed at the ends before it goes into the 'waiting' log line and the '::error::' line. A process can set its own comm with prctl(PR_SET_NAME) to up to 15 arbitrary bytes, including an embedded newline. That would start a new stdout line that the Actions runner reads as a workflow command, e.g. 'x\n::warning::y' (14 bytes). A '::' in the middle of a line does nothing, because commands are only recognised at the start of a line.
findings.evidence: comm of the process holding the lock -> processName() -> holderText() -> log() to stdout -> the runner parses each line for '::cmd::'. There's no reachable untrusted path. The only lock holders on a hosted runner are root apt/unattended-upgrades processes. Anyone who can start a process that holds /var/lib/dpkg/lock already runs code in the job and could print workflow commands directly. The wrapper's arguments come only from the checked-in ci.yml, not from event data.
findings.fix: Optional defence in depth: in processName(), replace control characters, e.g. `.replace(/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/g, '?')`, so that a name can never break the line.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. ci.yml changes only the two Playwright install run lines. Permissions, the action SHA pins and the step timeouts are unchanged. No ${{ }} expressions or event data reach the new run strings. apt-lock.js calls spawn(command, args) with an argv array, no shell option and the inherited env. That env is the same one retry.js already passes down, so there's no new environment exposure. Arguments come only from the checked-in workflow. parseArgs is strict, and usage errors exit 2 and fail closed. /proc/locks and /proc/<pid>/comm are read-only. The pid is a regex-parsed integer, so the comm path can't be traversed. A missing comm is handled. The wait is bounded by --wait-seconds, which must be finite and > 0, and the outer retry timeout still applies. A missing /proc/locks (non-Linux) skips the wait. That fails open only for the lock wait, which is acceptable. Tests use mkdtemp and clean up, and the real-flock test runs only on Linux CI. No new dependencies (package.json and lock unchanged). One MINOR: comm is not stripped of control characters before logging, but there's no reachable path to exploit it.
